label: GSAP
plainSummary: A JavaScript animation library that moves things on the page smoothly with precise timing and easing.
whyUsed: GSAP gives fine control over timing, easing, and sequencing that plain CSS makes awkward, and it works the same in every browser.

topics.label: What GSAP is and when to use it
gsap.to(), from(), fromTo() — the three basic moves

label: GSAP Timelines
plainSummary: A way to chain several animations so they play in sequence or overlap, controlled as one unit.

topics.label: Creating a timeline and adding tweens

label: ScrollTrigger
plainSummary: Ties animations to scroll position — things animate as you scroll down the page.
whyUsed: Scroll-driven reveals need to know exactly where an element is relative to the viewport; ScrollTrigger handles that math and the edge cases.

label: GSAP in React
plainSummary: Using GSAP safely inside React components, where elements get created and destroyed.

topics.label: Cleaning up animations when components unmount

label: GSAP Plugins
plainSummary: Add-ons for GSAP: Flip for layout transitions, Draggable for drag interactions, SplitText for per-letter effects, and more.

label: CSS animations
plainSummary: Making elements move or change using only stylesheets: @keyframes define the steps, `animation` plays them.
whyUsed: For simple, self-contained motion CSS is lighter than a JavaScript library and keeps styling and motion together.

label: CSS transitions
plainSummary: Smoothly animating a style change (like a hover color) instead of snapping instantly.

label: CSS transforms
plainSummary: Moving, scaling, and rotating elements without affecting the layout around them — the fastest properties to animate.

topics.label: Why transform and opacity animate smoothly

label: Web Animations API
plainSummary: The browser's built-in JavaScript animation engine (element.animate()), the thing libraries like GSAP build on.

label: Reduced motion preference
plainSummary: Respecting the user's operating-system setting that asks websites to minimize animation.
whyUsed: Motion can cause discomfort for some people; honoring the preference is an accessibility requirement.

label: IntersectionObserver
plainSummary: A browser feature that tells you when an element scrolls into view — the usual trigger for reveal-on-scroll effects.

topics.label: Observing elements and reacting when they appear

label: HTML
plainSummary: The language that defines a page's structure and content: headings, paragraphs, links, images.

label: Semantic HTML
plainSummary: Using tags that describe meaning (<nav>, <main>, <article>, <button>) instead of generic <div>s, so browsers and assistive tech understand the page.

label: CSS
plainSummary: The language that controls how a page looks: colors, fonts, spacing, layout.

topics.label: The box model: margin, border, padding
Cascade and specificity: which rule wins

label: CSS variables (design tokens)
plainSummary: Named values like --surface or --ease-snap that are defined once and reused everywhere, so a single change updates the whole site.
whyUsed: Tokens keep colors, spacing, and timing consistent and make theme changes trivial.

topics.label: Organising tokens as a design system

label: Flexbox
plainSummary: A layout system for arranging items in a row or column and controlling spacing and alignment.

resources.title: CSS-Tricks: A complete guide to Flexbox

label: CSS Grid
plainSummary: A two-dimensional layout system for rows and columns — ideal for page layouts and card grids.

resources.title: CSS-Tricks: A complete guide to Grid

label: Responsive design & media queries
plainSummary: Applying different styles depending on screen size or user preferences so a site works on phones and desktops.

label: JavaScript
plainSummary: The programming language that makes web pages interactive.

label: TypeScript
plainSummary: JavaScript with type labels that catch mistakes before the code runs. Files end in .ts / .tsx.
whyUsed: Types act like guardrails — the editor can flag a wrong value immediately instead of failing later in the browser.

topics.label: interface and type for shapes of data

label: The DOM
plainSummary: The live tree of everything on the page that JavaScript can find, read, and change.

topics.label: Listening for clicks and other events

label: Async JavaScript
plainSummary: Handling things that take time (network requests, timers) without freezing the page, using promises and async/await.

label: Imports & modules
plainSummary: Splitting code into files and pulling pieces in with import/export.

label: Fetching data (APIs)
plainSummary: Asking a server for data from JavaScript with fetch(), and reading the JSON that comes back.

label: JSON
plainSummary: A plain-text format for structured data using braces and quotes; used for settings files and API responses.

label: React
plainSummary: A library for building user interfaces out of reusable components that re-render when data changes.

label: React hooks
plainSummary: Functions like useState and useEffect that let components remember values and react to changes.

label: Astro
plainSummary: A framework for content-focused websites that ships plain HTML by default and only adds JavaScript where needed.

label: Next.js
plainSummary: A React framework that adds pages, routing, server rendering, and API routes.

label: Tailwind CSS
plainSummary: A styling approach where you compose small utility classes (flex, p-4, text-lg) directly in markup.

label: Vite & bundlers
plainSummary: Tools that turn your many source files into the optimized files a browser loads, with a fast local dev server.

label: Node.js
plainSummary: JavaScript running outside the browser — on your computer or a server — used for build tools and scripts.

label: Git basics
plainSummary: Saving checkpoints of your project (commits) and seeing what changed (status, diff, log).
whyUsed: Every safe workflow starts with knowing what changed and being able to undo it.

topics.label: The mental model: working tree, staging, commits

label: Branches & merging
plainSummary: Working on separate lines of history and combining them back together.

label: GitHub & remotes
plainSummary: Syncing your local checkpoints with an online copy (push) and getting others' changes (pull).

label: .gitignore
plainSummary: Telling git which files to leave out of history — downloaded packages, build output, secrets.

topics.label: Ignore patterns and what belongs in them

label: npm & packages
plainSummary: Downloading reusable code others wrote (packages) and recording which ones your project needs.
whyUsed: Almost every capability — an animation library, a UI kit — arrives as a package.

label: package.json & scripts
plainSummary: The project's manifest: its name, dependencies, and named shortcut commands like npm run dev.

label: Terminal basics
plainSummary: Typing commands to move around folders, list files, and run programs.

topics.label: cd, ls, pwd: where am I?

label: Shell scripting
plainSummary: Combining terminal commands into small programs with variables, loops, and conditions.

label: Searching code (ripgrep & regex)
plainSummary: Finding text across every file in a project, and writing search patterns (regular expressions).

topics.label: rg pattern path and useful flags (-n, -i, -g)

label: Environment variables & secrets
plainSummary: Named settings (often API keys) kept outside the code, usually in a .env file that is never committed.

label: Markdown
plainSummary: A lightweight way to write formatted text with plain characters — used for READMEs, docs, plans, and agent skills.

label: YAML & frontmatter
plainSummary: An indentation-based settings format, often placed between --- lines at the top of Markdown files.

label: Component architecture
plainSummary: Breaking an interface into reusable pieces (Card, Button, Hero) that each own their markup, style, and behavior.

label: Accessibility (a11y)
plainSummary: Making sure everyone can use the site — keyboard users, screen-reader users, people sensitive to motion.

topics.label: Keyboard focus and visible focus states

label: Automated testing
plainSummary: Writing small checks that run automatically to confirm code still behaves after changes.

label: Linting & formatting
plainSummary: Automatic proofreading (lint) and tidying (format) so code stays consistent and obvious mistakes are flagged.

topics.label: ESLint and Prettier: what each does

label: HTTP & APIs
plainSummary: How programs talk over the web: requests, responses, status codes like 200 and 404, and JSON payloads.

label: Local dev servers
plainSummary: Previewing your site on your own machine at an address like localhost:4321 while you work.

resources.title: MDN: What is a web server?

label: Browser DevTools & testing in the browser
plainSummary: Inspecting a live page — computed styles, console errors, element positions — and automating a browser to verify behavior.

label: How the Cursor agent works
plainSummary: The agent reads files, searches, runs commands, and edits code in a loop of tool calls until your request is done.

topics.label: The tool-call loop: read → decide → act
Agent mode vs Plan mode vs Ask mode

label: Skills & rules
plainSummary: Reusable instruction files (SKILL.md, .mdc rules) that teach the agent how to do specific tasks your way.

topics.label: What a skill is and when the agent reads one

label: Hooks, MCP & plugins
plainSummary: Ways to extend the agent: hooks run scripts at moments in its loop, MCP connects outside services as tools, plugins bundle these up.

topics.label: Hooks: observe or gate agent actions
MCP servers as tools (Figma, Slack, databases)

label: Editor extensions
plainSummary: Add-ons built with the VS Code extension API that give Cursor new panels, commands, and views.

topics.label: Webviews: HTML panels inside the editor

label: Figma design-to-code
plainSummary: Turning a Figma design into working components, or pushing code back into Figma, using the Figma MCP tools.

topics.label: Reading design context and mapping to components

label: Databases & SQL
plainSummary: Storing structured data in tables and asking questions of it with SQL.
